AAPL.rationale: Apple's fundamental health is strong: Q2 FY2026 delivered a March-quarter record $111.2B revenue with +16.6% YoY growth and $2.01 EPS (+21.8% YoY), while Services hit a record $31B at ~76% gross margin. The balance sheet is solid with $106.5B equity and manageable $82.7B debt (0.78x D/E). However, the trajectory shows clear QoQ deceleration (-22.7% revenue, -29.2% EPS) as expected from seasonal Q1-to-Q2 patterns, and the stock has rallied +25.1% in the past quarter to $333.26, pushing the P/E to 40.0x — near the top of its 30.5-43.1x 12-month range and well above the 32.5x level from a year ago. The P/B of 46.1x is elevated. KeyBanc has downgraded to Underweight citing unproven AI monetization and rising component costs. While the July 30 earnings report (consensus ~$1.89 EPS, +19.8% YoY) is a near-term catalyst, the stock is already priced for strong execution at a premium multiple, leaving limited margin of safety. Regulatory risks (EU DMA, DOJ antitrust, Epic Games) and rising memory costs flagged by management on the last earnings call add headwinds. The score reflects a world-class franchise with excellent fundamentals but a stretched valuation that caps upside.
